title: Structure of the earth's atmosphere
competency: Describe the layers of the atmosphere and their characteristics.

keywords.def: The lowest layer of the atmosphere, up to 8–16 km, where all weather happens.
The layer from the tropopause to about 50 km, with a lot of ozone.
The layer up to 80–85 km; the coldest layer, where meteorites burn up.
The uppermost, very thin layer, where temperature rises with height. It holds the ionosphere and exosphere.
A gas in the stratosphere that absorbs the sun's ultraviolet radiation.

en.text: By temperature, the atmosphere has four layers. The troposphere (to 8–16 km) has all the weather and cools with height. The stratosphere (to 50 km) holds ozone that absorbs ultraviolet rays. The mesosphere (to 80–85 km) is the coldest and burns up meteorites. The thermosphere, with the ionosphere and exosphere, gets hotter with height.

screens.title: Outside the plane
screens.ask: An aeroplane flies at 11 km. Is the air outside hotter or colder than on the ground?
screens.after: Much colder. In the troposphere temperature falls as you go up. At 11 km it can be about −55°C.

screens.title: Figure 1.9: the layers, bottom to top
items: Sea level to 8–16 km. All weather. Temperature falls with height. Top: tropopause with jet streams.
To about 50 km. Ozone absorbs ultraviolet rays, so it warms with height. Top: stratopause.
To 80–85 km. Coldest layer, near −100°C. Strongest winds. Meteorites burn up. Top: mesopause.
Uppermost, very thin. Temperature rises to 725–1,225°C. Has the ionosphere and exosphere.
80 to 500–700 km. Charged particles reflect radio waves.
Beyond 500–700 km. More hydrogen and helium.

screens.title: Four layers
paras: The atmosphere is divided into four layers by temperature changes.
They are the troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere and thermosphere.
The troposphere holds three-fourths of the atmosphere's mass.
